requirement_text: Harvard requires the SAT or ACT to meet its standardized testing requirement.
researcher_notes:
OPERATIVE POLICY AS OF RETRIEVAL: this is the live, current, present-tense statement on Harvard's dedicated testing FAQ and on the Application Requirements / First-Year Applicants / International Applicants / QuestBridge pages (all fetched 2026-08-21, all consistent with each other, none carry a cycle-year qualifier — this is an evergreen 'now' statement). Corroborating history from Harvard's own news coverage and press: testing was reinstated beginning with the Class of 2029 (Fall 2025 entry, announced April 2024), remained required for the Class of 2030 (Fall 2026 entry, admitted March 2026), and every live requirements page checked today states it as a current, unconditional requirement with no stated end date. Cross-referenced per task instruction to REQ-2026-08-21-HAR0002, a genuinely live official page on the same domain that states the OPPOSITE (test-optional) for a named past cycle. Recording this pair as CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE per instruction rather than silently treating HAR0002 as obviously superseded, even though that is this researcher's own assessment — see HAR0002 for why the conflict is nonetheless real (no superseding banner on that page).

RESOLUTION 2026-08-22 (see docs/research/requirement-conflicts/03-harvard-standardized-testing-policy.md): NOT A FACTUAL CONFLICT. HAR0002 scopes itself, in its own first sentence, to 'the 2021-2022 application cycle', which closed in 2022 — a statement about a closed cycle cannot contradict a statement about now. Supersession is dated and specific: Harvard announced on 11 April 2024 that standardized testing is required beginning with the Class of 2029 (Fall 2025 entry), ending test-optional. This FAQ re-fetched 2026-08-22 and unchanged: 'Harvard requires the SAT or ACT', no end date, with narrow accessibility exceptions (AP/IB/A-Level/national leaving exams) for students who genuinely cannot access the tests. This row reflects operative policy.

requirement_text: Due to the continuing COVID-19 pandemic, Harvard College is extending our standardized testing policy through the 2021-2022 application cycle. We will allow students to apply for admission without requiring ACT or SAT test results.
limitations: This page is dated 29 January 2021 and its own text scopes the claim to the '2021-2022 application cycle' (Fall 2022 entry) — a cycle that closed in 2022. As of retrieval (2026-08-21) the page is still live on the primary official domain with NO archived/superseded banner and NO pointer to the current policy page. This is the exact trap named in this lane's brief: a live official page that could be mistaken for still-governing policy. Contrast: a sibling page at college.harvard.edu/about/news-announcements/admission-application-considerations-class-2025 (an even older, March 2020 announcement) DOES carry a self-correcting notice — 'For the most up-to-date testing policies, please check this page on application requirements' — so Harvard's practice of adding superseding notices exists but was not applied to this particular page.
researcher_notes:
Cross-referenced to REQ-2026-08-21-HAR0001 (current requirement: SAT/ACT required, no expiration stated). Recorded as CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE per explicit task instruction rather than silently resolved to VERIFIED_HISTORICAL, even though this researcher's own reading is that the page is self-evidently about a closed cycle (title and first sentence both name '2021-2022'). Do not let a future ingestion pass pick this record as 'more current' — it is not; HAR0001 reflects the operative policy at retrieval time. Kept and flagged rather than dropped because the page is real, official, and still live with no disclaimer.

RESOLUTION 2026-08-22 (see docs/research/requirement-conflicts/03-harvard-standardized-testing-policy.md): SUPERSEDED, not competing — but the HAZARD is real and re-confirmed. This page's own text limits it to the 2021-2022 cycle, and Harvard's 11 April 2024 announcement reinstating testing from the Class of 2029 supersedes it by a dated action. Re-fetched 2026-08-22: the page is STILL LIVE on the primary official domain with NO superseding banner and no pointer to current policy, while a sibling March 2020 announcement does carry one. Any ingestion preferring 'official domain' without checking for a cycle scope stated in the page's own text would ingest this and tell a student Harvard is test-optional — an error that would cause a student not to sit the SAT. Keep this row and its verbatim text: the page being live IS the finding.

requirement_text: Although you are not required to take an English proficiency exam (such as the TOEFL, IELTS, etc.), you may submit scores if you wish to do so.
researcher_notes: A strong knowledge of English is still described as essential for successful study, but no test score is required to demonstrate it. Companion fact (HAR0004) records that TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo specifically cannot be used as a substitute for the SAT/ACT requirement — the two facts are easy to conflate ('no English test required' vs 'an English test cannot satisfy the standardized-testing requirement') and are recorded separately on purpose.

requirement_text: English language proficiency examinations such as the TOEFL, IELTS and Duolingo cannot be used to meet the standardized testing requirement.
researcher_notes: See HAR0003: distinct from whether an English-proficiency exam is itself required (it is not).

requirement_text: In exceptional cases when applicants are unable to access the SAT or ACT, Harvard will instead accept AP exam results, IB Actual or Predicted Scores, GCSE/A-Level Actual or Predicted Results, or National Leaving Exams Results (externally assessed) or Predictions.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary: the alternative-test list was reconstructed from a bulleted page layout, not a single quoted sentence. Re-read the source before showing this list to a student as a direct quotation.
researcher_notes: 'Exceptional cases' is Harvard's own qualifier — this is not a general alternative-test menu, it applies only when SAT/ACT access is genuinely blocked (cost or availability). Applies identically to QuestBridge Match applicants per college.harvard.edu/admissions/apply/questbridge ('Harvard requires the SAT or ACT test for every applicant... with limited exceptions... This standard applies uniformly regardless of application pathway — QuestBridge, Restrictive Early Action, or Regular Decision').

requirement_text: Students may self report their standardized test scores. Admitted students who decide to enroll at Harvard College and have submitted self-reported ACT or SAT test scores will be required to submit official test scores at the time of enrollment.
The study of English for four years: close and extensive reading of the classics of the world's literature.
limitations: Harvard states this is a recommended preparatory program, not a formulaic admission requirement — holistic review applies and 'there is no one size fits all rule.' Do not evaluate as a hard pass/fail gate.

requirement_text: The study of mathematics for four years. Calculus is not a requirement for admission to Harvard; students can still pursue quantitative fields by starting with an introductory calculus class that has no high school calculus prerequisite.
limitations: Harvard states this is a recommended preparatory program, not a formulaic admission requirement — holistic review applies and 'there is no one size fits all rule.' Do not evaluate as a hard pass/fail gate.
researcher_notes: Named-exclusion-shaped fact in reverse: most peer institutions imply calculus is expected of competitive applicants; Harvard's own page explicitly disclaims it as a requirement. Do not let a scoring/evaluation layer silently treat 'no calculus' as disqualifying.

requirement_text: The study of science for four years: physics, chemistry, and biology, and preferably one of these at an advanced level.
limitations: Harvard states this is a recommended preparatory program, not a formulaic admission requirement — holistic review applies and 'there is no one size fits all rule.' Do not evaluate as a hard pass/fail gate.

requirement_text: The study of history for at least two years, and preferably three years: American history, European history, and one additional advanced history course.
limitations: Harvard states this is a recommended preparatory program, not a formulaic admission requirement — holistic review applies and 'there is no one size fits all rule.' Do not evaluate as a hard pass/fail gate.

requirement_text: Four years of a single foreign language.
limitations: Harvard states this is a recommended preparatory program, not a formulaic admission requirement — holistic review applies and 'there is no one size fits all rule.' Do not evaluate as a hard pass/fail gate.
researcher_notes: 'A single foreign language' — page emphasizes depth in one language over breadth across several; worth preserving as its own clause rather than flattening to a bare '4 years' figure.

requirement_text: Common Application personal essay, plus five required Harvard-specific short-answer questions (150-word limit each): (1) Harvard has long recognized the importance of enrolling a student body with a diversity of perspectives and experiences. How will the life experiences that shaped who you are today enable you to contribute to Harvard? (2) Describe a time when you strongly disagreed with someone about an idea or issue. How did you communicate or engage with this person? What did you learn from this experience? (3) Briefly describe any of your extracurricular activities, employment experience, travel, or family responsibilities that have shaped who you are. (4) How do you hope to use your Harvard education in the future? (5) Top 3 things your roommates might like to know about you.
researcher_notes: All five short-answer questions are required; none are optional/pick-one.

requirement_text: Two teacher evaluations are required, from teachers who taught the applicant in different academic subjects.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary — re-read the source before quoting this to a student verbatim.
researcher_notes: Additional (optional) letters of recommendation may be submitted after initial application submission per the same page.

requirement_text: A School Report (including the counselor's letter and an official transcript) is required from the applicant's school. A Midyear School Report with first-semester/trimester senior-year grades is also required once available; a Final School Report is required only from admitted students who enroll.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary — re-read the source before quoting this to a student verbatim.

requirement_text: In most cases the Admissions Committee has sufficient information in the application materials to reach a decision without an interview. It is not possible to request an interview. When possible, Harvard tries to arrange for applicants to meet with alumni/ae in or near their school communities; in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. an alumnus/a contacts the applicant directly if an interview is possible, and elsewhere Harvard aims to hold one 'when and where possible.' The absence of an interview will not adversely affect an applicant's candidacy.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary combining language from the international-applicant interview FAQ with the general first-year-applicant guidance; re-read both sources before quoting verbatim.
researcher_notes: No interview is offered to transfer applicants at all, per a separate FAQ ('Are there interviews for transfer applicants?').

requirement_text: If you are applying to Harvard under Restrictive Early Action, you may not apply to any other private institution under an Early Decision, Early Action, or Restrictive Early Action plan, or to a binding early program at a public university. You cannot apply to another college's binding early decision program until Harvard has released Restrictive Early Action decisions in mid-December. After receiving Harvard's REA notification, including a deferral, applicants are free to apply to any institution under any plan, including binding programs such as Early Decision II. Applicants may still apply to public universities, military academies, and international universities under non-binding programs while an REA application to Harvard is pending, and may apply for scholarships or special academic programs with an early deadline elsewhere if the timing is a necessary aspect of consideration and the outcome is non-binding.
researcher_notes: Restrictive Early Action (REA) ITSELF is explicitly non-binding — Harvard's own page states 'a non-binding early program, signifying that if admitted, you are not obligated to attend, and have until May 1 to reply to our offer of admission.' What is binding/restrictive is the EXCLUSIVITY: which other early programs the applicant may not simultaneously pursue. Do not conflate REA's non-binding admission outcome with the binding-on-conduct restriction captured in this record — they are two different facts about the same plan. This is a contractual exclusivity restriction (the REA admission decision itself is non-binding, but the applicant is contractually restricted from applying early elsewhere while it is pending) — not a simple checkable eligibility fact. Should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule pass/fail threshold by a future interpretation pass (e.g. interpret-requirement.ts); needs human review to represent correctly.

requirement_text: Harvard is a QuestBridge National College Match partner. Those who rank Harvard and match are expected to enroll. Students who rank Harvard must be certain of their commitment to attend if matched, as the National College Match process is binding.
researcher_notes: Confirmed recent addition to Harvard's admission pathways: Harvard joined QuestBridge in January 2025, with the Class of 2030 (Fall 2026 entry) the first eligible cohort (per contemporaneous Harvard Crimson reporting; not itself an official-domain source, used here only to date the program's introduction, not to source the binding-commitment fact, which is quoted directly from Harvard's own page above). QuestBridge Match is a genuinely BINDING commitment to enroll, structurally different from Harvard's own REA (non-binding) — do not merge these two early pathways into one 'early admission' requirement row; they carry opposite binding status. This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact — should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review to represent correctly.

requirement_text: Harvard requires the SAT or ACT test for every applicant, with limited exceptions for AP scores, IB results, or international exams in cases of documented hardship. This standard applies uniformly regardless of application pathway — QuestBridge, Restrictive Early Action, or Regular Decision.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary — re-read the source before quoting this to a student verbatim.
researcher_notes: Confirms HAR0001's testing requirement is not bypassed by applying through QuestBridge.

requirement_text: Harvard's financial aid policies apply equally to all students regardless of citizenship. Admissions decisions are made without regard to whether an applicant has applied for financial assistance. Foreign students have the same access to financial aid funding as U.S. citizens.
researcher_notes: This is the specific, explicit extension of need-blind admission to international applicants the task brief asked to verify (many peer institutions are need-blind for domestic applicants only). Corroborated by the general Financial Aid Fact Sheet: 'A lack of financial resources or need for financial aid are not impediments to your admission' + 'Foreign students have the same access to financial aid funding as U.S. citizens' (https://college.harvard.edu/guides/financial-aid-fact-sheet, same retrieval date). Neither page uses the literal phrase 'need-blind,' but both state the operational content of a need-blind policy and both explicitly include international/foreign students rather than staying silent on citizenship.

requirement_text: You'll never be required to take on loans. [Optional loans exist as an additional aid type students may choose.] Since you are not a US citizen or permanent resident, you are not eligible for any federal financial aid funds and may only work on-campus. While long-term financing plans are designed primarily for US citizens, you or your parents may be eligible to participate under certain conditions.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary combining three separate pages (Affordability; Financial Aid Fact Sheet; Understanding Your Financial Aid Award - International Students) — re-read all three before quoting verbatim. The 'never required to take on loans' statement itself is general/institution-wide and not citizenship-scoped on the page it appears on. The international-specific award guide (https://college.harvard.edu/guides/understanding-your-financial-aid-award-international-students) does NOT itself restate the no-loan-required guarantee — it only confirms federal aid ineligibility (expected, since federal aid is a US-citizenship program, not a Harvard policy) and says optional long-term financing/loan programs are 'designed primarily for US citizens' with conditional international eligibility. This is a genuine partial gap, not a contradiction: no Harvard page found says the no-loan-REQUIRED guarantee does NOT apply to international students, but no international-specific page affirmatively restates it either — the guarantee is only stated on citizenship-neutral pages. Recorded as-is rather than resolved either optimistically or pessimistically.
researcher_notes: Directly responsive to task brief's instruction to check whether Harvard's no-loan policy explicitly extends to international applicants: the answer is 'implicitly, via a citizenship-neutral general statement, not via an explicit international-specific restatement' — see limitations.

requirement_text: If the admissions application fee presents a hardship for you or your family and you plan on applying for financial aid, the fee will be waived.
researcher_notes: Exact current fee amount (reported elsewhere as $95) was not found stated in-page during this pass; not recorded as a verbatim figure to avoid citing an unconfirmed number. Fee-waiver policy itself is directly sourced and confirmed.

requirement_text: We accept the Common Application. / For all first-year and transfer applicants, your first step will be to fill out and submit an application. You can do so through the Common Application.
limitations: Some third-party sources claim Harvard also accepts the Coalition Application by Scoir; this was NOT found stated on any official college.harvard.edu page checked in this pass (application-requirements, admissions/apply, first-year-applicants). Not recorded as accepted, per the lane rule against publishing unverified secondary-source claims — but also not recorded as explicitly excluded, since no official page states a platform exclusion either. QuestBridge Finalists use a separate QuestBridge-specific form instead of the Common App (see HAR0017 requirement and the QuestBridge deadline records).
